title: Heterogeneous Patch Orchestration and Forensic Evidence Playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook describes a repeatable, low-risk process for orchestrating software patches and runtime configuration updates across heterogeneous private deployments (VPC and on-prem), while ensuring a forensic-grade evidence trail suitable for customer audits and incident investigations. It targets field operator teams, SREs, and customer success engineers responsible for day-2 operations and upgrade rollouts.

Scope
-----
- Applies to Redwood Private and Dedicated customer deployments where operators manage control-plane or runtime binaries, model artifacts, quantized weights, or security-sensitive configuration changes.
- Covers staged rollout orchestration, automated and manual rollback, telemetry/evidence capture, retention policy, and post-change validation.
- Excludes hardware firmware upgrades (separate HW EOL playbooks) and network provider-level routing changes (see network playbooks).

Why this matters
----------------
Private deployments vary in hardware (A100, H100, RDMA fabrics), runtime config, and customer policy. A single blind patch can create subtle tokenization changes, KV cache drift, or service-level regressions. This playbook reduces blast radius by:

- Enforcing compatibility and safety gates before push
- Standardizing evidence capture for auditability (artifacts, digests, traces)
- Providing clear rollback criteria tied to SLOs and telemetry thresholds

Roles and ownership
-------------------
- Patch Lead (owner): coordinates rollout, signs off preflight checks, approves canary to production progression.
- Operator (field/on-call): executes playbook steps for assigned region/tenant.
- SRE (telemetry owner): validates observability configuration, determines anomaly windows and thresholds.
- Security Liaison: confirms cryptographic signatures and KMS operations succeeded.
- Customer Success (CS): notifies customer and collects customer-specific evidence/consent requirements where applicable.

Preconditions and prerequisites
-------------------------------
1. Artifact and image pipeline produces signed artifacts (SHA256) and an attestation manifest.
2. Preflight test harness run: offline smoke tests, deterministic eval prompt set, and KV-cache migration simulation.
3. Telemetry hooks present and validated: request tracing (trace id), token-level latency, error counts, and model output sampling.
4. Capacity buffer of >= 20% reserved or approved burst policy available for rollback spindown.
5. Backup snapshot available: stateful KV snapshot + model artifact versioned archive.

Preflight checklist (must pass before any canary)
- Artifact signature verified: sha256 matches signed manifest.
- Compatibility matrix check: runtime ABI, quantization profile, kernel availability.
- Smoke tests green: container start, gRPC health, simple generation for 10 prompt seeds.
- Telemetry sanity: sampling enabled, ingestion pipeline healthy, retention target set to 90 days for audit artifacts.
- Customer approval noted (if required) and CS notified of maintenance window.

Staged rollout workflow
----------------------
1. Canary (single-tenant or single-zone): deploy to 1 operator node or non-critical tenant.
   - Duration: minimum 30 minutes, recommended 2 hours for production traffic patterns.
   - Observability: high-sample tracing and compare canary vs baseline.
2. Small cohort (5–10% capacity): expand to limited tenants across zones.
3. Regional ramp: 25% capacity, across availability zones/edge sites.
4. Global sweep: full production.

For each stage perform:
- Automated validation suite (PASS/FAIL) with explicit metrics listed below.
- Evidence snapshot: store artifact digest, deployment manifest, and snapshot of relevant dashboards.
- Safety wait: minimum quiesce time (see SLO window table).

SLOs and acceptance thresholds
-----------------------------
| Metric | Baseline | Acceptable delta | Action on breach |
|--------|----------|------------------|------------------|
| 95th latency (inference, ms) | 120ms | +20% | Pause rollout, investigate
| Error rate (5m) | 0.5% | x3 absolute or >2% | Rollback to previous artifact
| Token-level throughput (rps) | baseline | -15% | Evaluate batching and fallback paths
| Model quality (prompt eval loss/metric) | reference eval | drop >2% | Halt and triage with Research/Applied ML

Forensic evidence capture (what to collect)
-------------------------------------------
Collect and store these items in the evidence bucket (immutable, write-once if possible):
- Signed artifact manifest (SHA256, signer identity, timestamp).
- Deployment manifest: kube yaml / operator plan, tenant mapping, node list.
- Preflight test logs and deterministic eval outputs (seeded prompts + model outputs).
- Telemetry snapshots: traces (sampled), request-level logs for the canary window, per-route latency histograms.
- KV-cache and session-state snapshot checksums (if applicable).
- Git commit hash and CI build id for the runtime and orchestration code.
- Operator execution log (who ran what CLI, with timestamps).
- KMS audit entries for any key unwrap/sign operations.

Retention and tagging policy
---------------------------
- Default retention for patch evidence: 90 days.
- For regulated customers or CS-requested evidence, extend to customer SLA (e.g., 1 year).
- Tag evidence with: artifact-version, rollout-stage, region, tenant-id(s), operator-id, change-ticket-id.

Automated evidence pipeline (recipe)
----------------------------------
- On deploy: orchestration service posts a deployment-event to evidence service containing manifest and signatures.
- Evidence service pulls per-route telemetry window (t0..t1), gzips and stores in bucket under /evidence/{change-id}/telemetry.tar.gz.
- Store deterministic eval outputs under /evidence/{change-id}/evals/{seed-id}.json.
- Index metadata in the evidence catalog (searchable).

Commands / automation snippets
----------------------------
- Verify signature and manifest (example):
  shasum -a 256 runtime.tar.gz > runtime.sha256
  cat runtime.manifest | jq '.signature' | base64 -d | \\\
    openssl rsautl -verify -inkey /opt/keys/pub.pem -in -

- Take snapshot and upload evidence (operator agent):
  ./operator-agent snapshot --kv-checksum --trace-window 2026-02-14T12:00:00Z/2026-02-14T14:00:00Z \\
    --out s3://redwood-evidence/{change-id}/snapshot.tar.gz

Rollback criteria and procedure
------------------------------
Rollback triggers (any of the following):
1. Error rate breach (defined above).
2. Latency degradation beyond threshold for >3 consecutive 5-minute windows.
3. Model output quality regressions on deterministic prompt set.
4. Operator-detected data-corruption (KV mismatch checksums).

Rollback high-level steps:
1. Pause further rollouts and place change in HOLD state in orchestration console.
2. Execute rollback job to pin tenants/nodes back to previous artifact version. Use automation if safe: 
   - For stateless changes: fast rollback (seconds to minutes).
   - For stateful changes (KV schema changes): follow state rollback runbook and, if required, consult forensics team.
3. Preserve evidence from failed rollout window and mark it in catalog as "incident".
4. Communicate: notify customers (CS) according to SLA and incident comms templates.
5. Run post-rollback validation: sanity smoke tests, KV checksum validation, telemetry recovery check.

Rollback commands (example)
- Trigger rollback job:
  redwoodctl rollout rollback --change-id {change-id} --target previous --force-if-safe
- Confirm state:
  redwoodctl node status --filter change={change-id} | tee rollback-confirm.log

Failure modes and mitigations
----------------------------
- Hammering on dependency: If a runtime update increases memory usage and OOMs occur, mitigation is to drain nodes, scale up temporary capacity, and roll back. Evidence: OOM traces + dmesg logs.
- KV inconsistency after model swap: If per-tenant cache keys diverge, run the KV-reconciliation tool (operator utility) and hold on full rollout until reconciliation is complete.
- Telemetry pipeline outage masks regressions: If evidence service cannot collect traces, halt rollout and switch to manual artifact preservation + enhanced logging on operator hosts.

Post-mortem and continuous improvement
-------------------------------------
- If rollout results in an incident, initiate a 72-hour rapid triage with SRE, Patch Lead, Research, and CS.
- Required artifacts for post-mortem: evidence bundle, operator timeline, CI pipeline logs, and customer reports.
- Track action items in the continuous improvement tracker and include a changelog entry in the patch release notes.

Runbook run-through example (typical timeline)
-------------------------------------------
1. T-72h: Patch Lead publishes change ticket; CS and Security accept.
2. T-24h: Preflight tests run, golden evals compared, signatures validated.
3. T-0: Canary deploy starts to tenant T001, high-sample tracing enabled.
4. T+30m: Canary automated validations pass; evidence pipeline snapshots collected.
5. T+2h: Small cohort expansion; telemetry indicates 8% latency increase -> HOLD.
6. T+3h: SRE traces root cause (kernel fallback path) -> rollback executed.
7. T+3h15m: Rollback completes; post-rollback validation passes; evidence archived under change-id.
8. T+24h: Post-mortem scheduled; remediation plan created.

Appendices
----------
Appendix A — Evidence naming convention example:
- {change-id}_{region}_{stage}_artifact-{sha256}.tar.gz

Appendix B — SLO windows and sample sizes:
- Canary: 30–120 minutes, sample 1000 requests or all requests if fewer.
- Cohort: 2–6 hours, sample 10,000 requests.
- Regional: 6–24 hours, sample 50,000 requests.

Appendix C — Quick links and references:
- Operator toolkit: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/private-deploy-operator-cheat-sheet-for-field-installations-2027
- Rollback procedures: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/operator-sentinel-escrow-and-durable-rollback-procedures-2026
- Telemetry playbook: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/post-installation-telemetry-and-acceptance-checklist-2026

Owner and maintenance
---------------------
Owner: Patch Lead (oncall-rotation: eng-private-deployments-patch-leads)
Review cadence: annual or after any major incident.

Contact
-------
For questions or to request customer-specific evidence retention changes, contact the Patch Lead via PagerDuty and file a ticket in the private-deployments change queue.
